tracks.title: Foundations
tracks.kicker: The AWS the contact center sits on
tracks.why: A flow fails in IAM, a Region, a log group, or a network rule long before it fails as a 'Connect bug'.

lessons.title: What Connect actually depends on
lessons.why: You cannot debug a contact center if you treat AWS as a logo on the invoice.

lessons.title: Regions, endpoints, and why Osaka is special
lessons.why: A Region is a capacity, latency, and residency boundary. It is not a checkbox you can flip on a live number.

lessons.title: IAM is not the security profile
lessons.why: Agents get a security profile. Automations get an IAM principal. Mixing the names produces a policy that cannot place a call and a user who can.

lessons.title: Lambda is a seam, not a place to hide a CRM
lessons.why: The flow will not wait for a slow system of record. Design the function for the timeout you actually have.

lessons.title: S3 holds the proof
lessons.why: Recordings, chat transcripts, exported reports, and attachments are objects. If the bucket policy is wrong, the contact still 'succeeds' and the file is missing.

lessons.title: Kinesis is how the ecosystem listens
lessons.why: Anything that must react to agents or to finished contacts needs a stream, not a person refreshing a report.

lessons.title: CloudWatch tells you the flow ran
lessons.why: Without flow logs you are guessing which block took the error branch.

lessons.title: The network path is part of the product
lessons.why: Connect's softphone is WebRTC in the agent's browser. A firewall designed for a desk phone will block it.

lessons.title: Certifications and the badges that are not certifications
lessons.why: There is no Amazon Connect specialty exam on the AWS Certification catalog. Pretending a badge is that exam misleads a hiring plan.

lessons.title: A depends-on map you can defend
lessons.why: Every later track names the foundation it needs. If that foundation is missing, the track's lab will show the same fault.

lessons.title: Feature timeline
lessons.why: Names moved. Features mostly stayed. Voice ID did not.

tracks.title: Instance
tracks.why: Every number, user, and flow lives in one instance in one Region. Get this wrong and the rest of the design has no home.

lessons.title: Create the instance on purpose
lessons.why: The instance is the tenancy boundary for users, flows, and numbers. An accidental second instance splits reports and identity.

lessons.title: SAML attributes that make a user real
lessons.why: A successful SAML login that lands without a routing profile is a user who cannot take a contact.

lessons.title: CloudFormation, CDK, and Terraform
lessons.why: Clicking the console does not review. A stack does.

lessons.title: Prompts, statuses, and the small quotas
lessons.why: The limits that surprise people are the ones marked not adjustable.

tracks.title: Telephony
tracks.why: Customers still dial a number. The number type decides the price, the carrier design, and the failure mode.

lessons.title: DID, toll-free, shared cost, UIFN
lessons.why: The number type is a cost and a failure-domain choice.

lessons.title: Claiming and the false 'limit' on the first number
lessons.why: The first claim is a Support conversation more often than people expect.

lessons.title: Porting without losing the rollback
lessons.why: A port is a date with the losing carrier. It is not a flow change.

lessons.title: SIP, external voice, and what is not a trunk in the CUCM sense
lessons.why: Connect does not give you a CUCM SIP trunk page. It gives you native telephony, transfers to numbers, and an external voice connector for analytics.

lessons.title: Outbound calls and caller ID
lessons.why: Outbound is a queue setting, a permission, and a country quota.

tracks.title: Contact flows
tracks.why: The flow is the product the caller hears. A missing error branch is a dropped call.

lessons.title: Flow types are not one canvas
lessons.why: Each flow type only offers the blocks that make sense there. A hold flow is not a place to transfer to a queue and hope.

lessons.title: The block catalog, grouped by job
lessons.why: You do not memorize fifty icons. You group them by the job they do.

lessons.title: Attributes are the only memory the next system gets
lessons.why: If it is not an attribute, the CRM, the whisper, and the CTR cannot see it.

lessons.title: Modules are how you stop copying flows
lessons.why: A copied inbound flow drifts. A module has one published body.

lessons.title: Every error branch is a product decision
lessons.why: An unconnected error output hangs up. That is a choice, even if you did not mean it.

lessons.title: The flow language is how instances share a design
lessons.why: The designer is a view. The JSON is what you review and promote.

tracks.title: Lex V2
tracks.why: Self-service only works if the intent you branch on is the intent Lex actually returned.

lessons.title: Get customer input is the Lex block
lessons.why: There is no separate 'Lex block' to hunt for. Get customer input is where the bot is selected.

lessons.title: Slots become attributes or they vanish
lessons.why: The agent cannot see a slot you did not copy.

lessons.title: Fallback is a route, not a failure
lessons.why: Callers who say something unexpected are still customers.

tracks.title: Agent assist and agentic AI
tracks.kicker: Q, Wisdom, and what replaced them
tracks.why: The names changed in 2023 and again in 2026. The IAM prefix and the block you configure did not move in lockstep.

lessons.title: Wisdom, Q, and agent assist are one lineage
lessons.why: Using the old name in a design review is fine. Using it as the only name in a 2026 runbook is not.

lessons.title: Turn on assist only where you can show the source
lessons.why: A generated sentence without a cited article is not knowledge. It is a guess in the agent's ear.

lessons.title: Agentic CX is a flow exit, not a magic queue
lessons.why: The application returns an exit condition. Your flow must have a branch for each one, including failure.

lessons.title: Voice ID has ended
lessons.why: On 14 October 2026 this feature is already past its end of support. Leave the blocks out.

tracks.title: Lambda
tracks.why: Most 'random' flow errors are a Lambda response that missed the timeout or the shape Connect accepts.

lessons.title: The response contract
lessons.why: Connect does not debug your function. It branches.

lessons.title: When the work is slower than eight seconds
lessons.why: Silence is a defect. Async plus a prompt is the pattern.

lessons.title: Association, resource policy, and the log that says AccessDenied
lessons.why: The flow log is telling the truth. The function never ran.

tracks.title: Routing
tracks.why: Priority and delay decide who is offered the contact. The queue name does not.

lessons.title: Queues wait. Profiles decide who is eligible.
lessons.why: A queue with nobody whose profile includes it is a silent parking lot.

lessons.title: Priority, delay, and concurrency
lessons.why: Lower priority number wins. Delay keeps a second team in reserve. Concurrency is how many of each channel an agent holds.

lessons.title: Hours and overrides
lessons.why: The check uses the queue's hours and the queue's time zone. Your laptop's clock is irrelevant.

lessons.title: Quick connects and the flows behind them
lessons.why: A quick connect is a target plus a flow. The flow is where you record, whisper, and set attributes.

tracks.title: CCP and workspace
tracks.why: If UDP 3478 is blocked, the agent is signed in and cannot hear the customer.

lessons.title: The CCP is a web app with a telephone inside
lessons.why: Sign-in can succeed when media cannot. Those are different allow lists.

lessons.title: The workspace is where the ecosystem becomes visible
lessons.why: Profiles, cases, views, and third-party apps belong here, not in a second monitor full of URLs.

lessons.title: Streams is the supported way to embed the CCP
lessons.why: If you must hide the CCP inside another app, use amazon-connect-streams. Do not scrape the page.

lessons.title: VDI, VPN, and the audio path
lessons.why: The browser that runs the CCP must be the browser whose network can reach TURN.

tracks.title: Profiles, cases, tasks
tracks.kicker: The work that outlives the call
tracks.why: A contact ends. A case, a task, and a profile are how the next person continues it.

lessons.title: Profiles are the customer, not the contact
lessons.why: The contact ends. The profile is how the next contact knows who called.

lessons.title: Cases survive the transfer
lessons.why: A case is the issue. Contacts are the attempts to close it.

lessons.title: Tasks are the channel with no audio
lessons.why: A promise to call back, a form to review, and a follow-up are tasks. They have quotas and an expiry.

lessons.title: One customer, three objects
lessons.why: Profile, case, and contact answer different questions. Collapsing them makes reporting lie.

tracks.title: Channels and campaigns
tracks.why: Each channel has its own quota, its own price unit, and its own way of getting stuck in an active state.

lessons.title: Chat, SMS, WhatsApp, and the idle-chat quota
lessons.why: A chat that has gone quiet is still an active chat. The default ceiling is 500, shared with SMS, WhatsApp, and Apple Messages for Business.

lessons.title: Email is a contact with a 90-day thread
lessons.why: An email is not a chat transcript and not a case, though it can create both.

lessons.title: Campaigns dial only after the quota is not zero
lessons.why: The default concurrent campaign call quota is 0. The symptom is a fast busy, and it is not a carrier outage.

lessons.title: In-app, web, and video
lessons.why: The customer does not dial. The widget starts a contact. You still pay for voice minutes plus the media type.

tracks.title: Analytics
tracks.why: You cannot staff, coach, or dispute a contact you cannot join back to one ContactId.

lessons.title: Read a CTR before you build a dashboard
lessons.why: The CTR is the finished contact. Real-time metrics are a picture of now. They answer different questions.

lessons.title: Real-time boards and historical intervals
lessons.why: Service level is a historical interval unless you say you are looking at the live queue.

lessons.title: Conversational analytics is Contact Lens under a new name
lessons.why: The function did not vanish on 4 August 2026. The admin guide changed the name.

lessons.title: Agent events are the live staffing truth
lessons.why: The real-time board is a view. The event stream is the feed other systems can trust.

tracks.title: Security, quotas, price
tracks.kicker: IAM, KMS, SAML, and the bill
tracks.why: A design that cannot name its IAM prefix, its key, and its quota will fail the first real week.

lessons.title: Encryption is a key policy
lessons.why: A customer-managed key you created and then forgot to share with Connect is an outage, not a security win.

lessons.title: SAML, least privilege, and the admin you forgot
lessons.why: Federation does not remove the need for a break-glass admin, and it does not make that admin safe.

lessons.title: Quotas are a project plan
lessons.why: The default numbers in the docs are for new accounts. Your account can be lower because defaults have changed over the years.

lessons.title: How to talk about the price without inventing it
lessons.why: The rate card is public and dated. An estimate that hides the date is a guess.

tracks.title: Global Resiliency
tracks.why: AWS supports one multi-Region pattern. A home-built second instance is not that pattern.

lessons.title: Only one multi-Region design is supported
lessons.why: AWS says Global Resiliency is the supported multi-Region approach, and that unsupported designs can affect quotas and the SLA story.

lessons.title: What a failover drill has to prove
lessons.why: A drill that only signs an admin in has not tested a customer call.

lessons.title: Migration patterns that survive contact with a Monday
lessons.why: The pattern is dual-run, a small number, evidence, then the rest. Heroic cutovers are how recordings go missing.

tracks.title: Troubleshooting
tracks.kicker: One fault, one log, one change
tracks.why: The useful habit is to name the hop, the ContactId, the counter, and the log line before you edit the flow.

lessons.title: Leg, id, counter, capture
lessons.why: The same four questions work on a CUCM trunk and on a Connect flow.

lessons.title: Audio quality is a path, not a codec myth
lessons.why: Connect's softphone does not ask you to pick G.711. The failures are path failures.

lessons.title: A flow log you can actually search
lessons.why: The query is short. The discipline is saving the ContactId before you hang up the test phone.

lessons.title: Faults worth memorizing
lessons.why: A short list beats a wiki nobody opens during an incident.

lessons.title: Failed to establish softphone connection
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the softphone hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: ice_collection_timeout
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the browser hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: One-way audio
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the media path hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Lambda AccessDenied in the flow log
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the invoke hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.why: This fault shows up at the lambda hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.why: This fault shows up at the telephony quota hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Fast busy on a campaign call
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the campaign quota hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Chat starts fail while agents look idle
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the chat quota hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.why: This fault shows up at the storage hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: SAML user has no routing profile
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the identity hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Caller hangs up on an error with no prompt
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the flow hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Transfer to queue does nothing useful
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the flow order hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: The overflow team takes every call
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the routing hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Replica Region has no numbers
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the resiliency hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Custom CCP loads and audio never starts
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the streams hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Error rate above 2 percent on the domain allow list
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the proxy hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: An email reply became a new contact
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the email hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Voice ID block fails in a 2026 flow
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the flow hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: TurnNlb does not resolve
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the dns hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: CCP shows available and the microphone is blocked
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the browser permission hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Midnight callers reach a closed queue that the prompt calls open
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the hours hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: A holiday still follows the weekly hours
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the override hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Lex works in its console and errors on the call
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the lex hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: The chat widget does not start
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the chat widget hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: The CUCM agent has a blank screen pop
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the transfer hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Salesforce pops the wrong person
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the screen pop hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: WFM adherence is blank on day one
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the wfm hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Analytics search returns nothing for a known call
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the analytics hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: A home agent's 911 address is the headquarters
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the e911 hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: The second WFM consumer is minutes behind
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the kinesis hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Outbound calls fail or show the wrong number
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the outbound hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Callbacks sit forever
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the callback hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: A failed ContactId has no flow log
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the logs hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Failover flows take the Lambda error branch
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the replica hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Failover plays silence where a prompt should be
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the prompts hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: New tasks will not route
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the tasks hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Every agent can play every recording
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the access hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

lessons.title: Distribute by percentage is being used as skills routing
lessons.why: This fault shows up at the routing hop. Naming it stops a team from editing the flow when the failure is elsewhere.

tracks.title: Bridge
tracks.kicker: From CUCM, UCCX, UCCE, Webex, Genesys, Avaya
tracks.why: Migrations fail when a skill group, a script, and a Finesse gadget are all called 'the queue'.

lessons.title: The mapping table you put in the migration pack
lessons.why: Names from the old platform are not Connect resources. Write the map before you build the queues.

lessons.title: A migration playbook
lessons.why: The order is identity, network, flows, a pilot number, reports, then the port.

lessons.title: Pitfalls that show up in every platform
lessons.why: The platforms differ. The mistakes repeat.

lessons.title: CUIC and the Connect report are different clocks
lessons.why: If you do not write both formulas, the business will say the new platform is slower or faster than it is.

tracks.title: Integrations
tracks.kicker: Salesforce, ServiceNow, Teams, CUCM beside Connect
tracks.why: The CRM, the PBX, and the chat client each own a different seam. Mixing them up builds a transfer that pops the wrong record.

lessons.title: Salesforce: CTI Adapter and SCC-AC
lessons.why: Voice stays on Connect. The question is which system owns the digital channels and the case.

lessons.title: ServiceNow Voice
lessons.why: ServiceNow can own assignment while Connect owns the conversation, if you map the queues on purpose.

lessons.title: Teams is a chat client in the published pattern
lessons.why: The AWS blog's Teams integration is not a SIP trunk into Teams Phone.

lessons.title: CUCM and Webex beside Connect
lessons.why: There is no AWS-managed CUCM CTI adapter in the docs this campus cites. The seam is the phone number.

tracks.title: Ecosystem
tracks.kicker: Glossary, mind map, WFM, recording, E911, CRM, AI
tracks.why: Connect answers the contact. Workforce, quality, emergency location, and the system of record sit beside it, and they only stay honest if they share ContactId.

lessons.title: The contact center is not the whole operation
lessons.why: WFM, quality, emergency location, and the CRM fail quietly when they are bolted on after go-live.

lessons.title: Glossary
lessons.why: A migration argument is usually two definitions of the same word.

lessons.title: Mind map
lessons.why: If you cannot point at the box that owns a function, you will build it twice.

lessons.title: Native forecasting and scheduling
lessons.why: Native WFM is in the product. Third-party WFM is justified when you already live in that suite, not because Connect 'cannot schedule'.

lessons.title: Third-party WFM configuration and faults
lessons.why: The integration is the agent event stream plus a historical extract. If either is late, adherence is fiction.

lessons.title: Recording and screen capture
lessons.why: If the object is not in S3, you do not have a recording, no matter what the flow block said.

lessons.title: Third-party recorders and live media
lessons.why: Some QM suites want the audio while the call is up. That is Kinesis Video Streams, not a second SIP trunk.

lessons.title: Quality management on top of analytics
lessons.why: A score without the recording is an opinion. A recording without a form is an archive.

lessons.title: Configure conversational analytics and fix the empty transcript
lessons.why: Analytics that is not enabled on the contact produces an empty search and a false 'the feature is down'.

lessons.title: E911 for agents on the CCP
lessons.why: A contact-center platform is not automatically an emergency-calling design. In the US Regions where this exists, you still have to store a real address.

lessons.title: CRM configuration and the faults that look like routing bugs
lessons.why: A wrong screen pop is often an attribute bug, not a Salesforce bug.

lessons.title: AI agents: configure, cite, and a way out
lessons.why: An agent who cannot reach a person is not assisted. They are stuck.

lessons.title: Integration maps
lessons.why: A map is a list of seams with a key on each line. A poster of logos is not a map.

lessons.title: Future hooks, not future rewrites
lessons.why: Add the next system on a hook that already exists. Do not scrape the CCP and do not fork the flow for every vendor.

foundations.title: Instance the contact center sits on
foundations.blurb: IAM, Lambda, S3, Kinesis, and CloudWatch are not inside the instance. This stack creates the instance and turns on flow logs and Contact Lens.
foundations.cfn:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: Connect instance with flow logs and Contact Lens
Resources:
  CampusInstance:
    Type: AWS::Connect::Instance
    Properties:
      IdentityManagementType: SAML
      InstanceAlias: campus-demo
      Attributes:
        InboundCalls: true
        OutboundCalls: true
        ContactflowLogs: true
        ContactLens: true

instance.title: AWS::Connect::Instance
instance.blurb: One instance, one Region. IdentityManagementType is SAML or CONNECT_MANAGED. The alias becomes the instance name.
instance.cfn:
Resources:
  CampusInstance:
    Type: AWS::Connect::Instance
    Properties:
      IdentityManagementType: CONNECT_MANAGED
      InstanceAlias: campus-demo
      Attributes:
        InboundCalls: true
        OutboundCalls: true
        ContactflowLogs: true

telephony.title: Claim a phone number
telephony.blurb: AWS::Connect::PhoneNumber claims a DID or toll-free number into the instance. The first claim can still fail a service quota even when the template is valid.
telephony.cfn:
Resources:
  PilotDid:
    Type: AWS::Connect::PhoneNumber
    Properties:
      TargetArn: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Arn
      CountryCode: US
      Type: DID
      Prefix: "+1503"

flows.title: Contact flow from flow-language JSON
flows.blurb: AWS::Connect::ContactFlow stores the flow-language document in Content. Type CONTACT_FLOW is the inbound flow. Build the JSON in the flow lab, then paste it here.
flows.cfn:
Resources:
  OrderStatus:
    Type: AWS::Connect::ContactFlow
    Properties:
      InstanceArn: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Arn
      Name: OrderStatus
      Type: CONTACT_FLOW
      Content: '{"Version":"2019-10-30","StartAction":"a1","Actions":[{"Identifier":"a1","Type":"MessageParticipant","Parameters":{"Text":"Thanks for calling."},"Transitions":{"NextAction":"a2","Errors":[],"Conditions":[]}},{"Identifier":"a2","Type":"DisconnectParticipant","Parameters":{},"Transitions":{}}]}'

lex.title: Associate a Lex V2 bot alias
lex.blurb: The bot must be associated with the instance before Get customer input can select it. IntegrationType is LEX_BOT and IntegrationArn is the alias ARN.
lex.cfn:
Resources:
  LexAlias:
    Type: AWS::Connect::IntegrationAssociation
    Properties:
      InstanceId: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Id
      IntegrationType: LEX_BOT
      IntegrationArn: arn:aws:lex:us-west-2:123456789012:bot-alias/BOTID/ALIASID

ai.title: Turn on Contact Lens with the instance
ai.blurb: Agent assist still uses the wisdom IAM prefix. The instance attribute ContactLens is the switch this campus can show in a template. The assistant domain is associated after the instance exists.
ai.cfn:
Resources:
  CampusInstance:
    Type: AWS::Connect::Instance
    Properties:
      IdentityManagementType: SAML
      InstanceAlias: campus-demo
      Attributes:
        InboundCalls: true
        OutboundCalls: true
        ContactflowLogs: true
        ContactLens: true

lambda.title: Allow Connect to invoke the function
lambda.blurb: Two pieces: a resource policy that trusts connect.amazonaws.com, and an integration association so the flow can select the function. The block still waits at most 8 seconds when InvocationType is SYNCHRONOUS.
lambda.cfn:
Resources:
  InvokePermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Ref FlowHook
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      Principal: connect.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Arn
  LambdaAssociation:
    Type: AWS::Connect::IntegrationAssociation
    Properties:
      InstanceId: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Id
      IntegrationType: LAMBDA_FUNCTION
      IntegrationArn: !GetAtt FlowHook.Arn

routing.title: Hours, queue, and routing profile
routing.blurb: Priority and delay live on the routing profile queue config, not on the queue name. Lower priority is offered first. Delay holds that queue back.
routing.cfn:
Resources:
  OfficeHours:
    Type: AWS::Connect::HoursOfOperation
    Properties:
      InstanceArn: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Arn
      Name: OfficeHours
      TimeZone: America/Los_Angeles
      Config:
        - Day: MONDAY
          StartTime: { Hours: 8, Minutes: 0 }
          EndTime: { Hours: 18, Minutes: 0 }
  OrdersQueue:
    Type: AWS::Connect::Queue
    Properties:
      InstanceArn: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Arn
      Name: Orders
      HoursOfOperationArn: !GetAtt OfficeHours.HoursOfOperationArn
  BasicProfile:
    Type: AWS::Connect::RoutingProfile
    Properties:
      InstanceArn: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Arn
      Name: Basic
      DefaultOutboundQueueArn: !GetAtt OrdersQueue.QueueArn
      MediaConcurrencies:
        - Channel: VOICE
          Concurrency: 1
      QueueConfigs:
        - QueueReference: { QueueArn: !GetAtt OrdersQueue.QueueArn, Channel: VOICE }
          Priority: 1
          Delay: 0

workspace.title: Approved origin for a custom CCP
workspace.blurb: A custom CCP using amazon-connect-streams has to be served from an origin you approve on the instance. The softphone still needs UDP 3478. Approving the origin does not open that port.
workspace.cfn:
Resources:
  CcpOrigin:
    Type: AWS::Connect::ApprovedOrigin
    Properties:
      InstanceId: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Id
      Origin: https://ccp.example.com

records.title: Case and profile are separate services
records.blurb: Profiles and cases use their own IAM prefixes. This template only shows the Connect instance those services attach to. Create the profile domain and the Cases domain in the same Region.
records.cfn:
Resources:
  CampusInstance:
    Type: AWS::Connect::Instance
    Properties:
      IdentityManagementType: SAML
      InstanceAlias: campus-demo
      Attributes:
        InboundCalls: true
        OutboundCalls: true
        ContactflowLogs: true

channels.title: Queue concurrency is per channel
channels.blurb: Chat, SMS, WhatsApp, and email do not share the voice concurrency of 1. Set MediaConcurrencies for the channel you are opening. Quotas for concurrent chats are still an instance limit.
channels.cfn:
Resources:
  ChatProfile:
    Type: AWS::Connect::RoutingProfile
    Properties:
      InstanceArn: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Arn
      Name: ChatAndVoice
      DefaultOutboundQueueArn: !GetAtt OrdersQueue.QueueArn
      MediaConcurrencies:
        - Channel: VOICE
          Concurrency: 1
        - Channel: CHAT
          Concurrency: 2

analytics.title: CTR stream and Contact Lens
analytics.blurb: Contact trace records leave the instance through AWS::Connect::InstanceStorageConfig. ResourceType CONTACT_TRACE_RECORDS and StorageType KINESIS_STREAM is the fan-out path. Contact Lens is an instance attribute plus the recording and analytics block in the flow.
analytics.cfn:
Resources:
  CtrStream:
    Type: AWS::Connect::InstanceStorageConfig
    Properties:
      InstanceArn: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Arn
      ResourceType: CONTACT_TRACE_RECORDS
      StorageType: KINESIS_STREAM
      KinesisStreamConfig:
        StreamArn: !GetAtt ContactStream.Arn

security.title: Instance-scoped IAM, not connect star
security.blurb: A security profile is not an IAM policy. This statement allows two read actions on one instance ARN. Lambda's resource policy is a separate document.
security.cfn:
Resources:
  OperatorPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - connect:DescribeInstance
              - connect:ListQueues
            Resource: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Arn

resiliency.title: Traffic distribution group
resiliency.blurb: Global Resiliency uses a traffic distribution group across a supported Region pair. Telephony percentage moves in steps of 10. A second instance you created by hand is not this resource.
resiliency.cfn:
Resources:
  Pair:
    Type: AWS::Connect::TrafficDistributionGroup
    Properties:
      Name: campus-pair
      InstanceArn: !GetAtt SourceInstance.Arn
      Description: Virginia source with an Oregon replica

troubleshoot.title: Flow logs have to be on
troubleshoot.blurb: The troubleshooting habit starts with a log line. ContactflowLogs on the instance is what lets Set logging behavior write to CloudWatch.
troubleshoot.cfn:
Resources:
  CampusInstance:
    Type: AWS::Connect::Instance
    Properties:
      IdentityManagementType: SAML
      InstanceAlias: campus-demo
      Attributes:
        InboundCalls: true
        OutboundCalls: true
        ContactflowLogs: true

bridge.title: The Connect objects a migration creates
bridge.blurb: CUCM, UCCX, and UCCE have no CloudFormation resource in this API. The objects you create on the Connect side are the queue, the routing profile, and the hours. Map the old skill group onto those, not onto a single queue name.
bridge.cfn:
Resources:
  MigratedQueue:
    Type: AWS::Connect::Queue
    Properties:
      InstanceArn: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Arn
      Name: BillingSkill
      HoursOfOperationArn: !GetAtt OfficeHours.HoursOfOperationArn
      Description: Was a UCCE skill group. Priority now lives on the routing profile.

integrations.title: Lambda hook for a screen pop
integrations.blurb: Salesforce and ServiceNow do not receive contact attributes unless you write them and call out. The association is what lets the flow invoke the function that sets the customer id.
integrations.cfn:
Resources:
  PopAssociation:
    Type: AWS::Connect::IntegrationAssociation
    Properties:
      InstanceId: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Id
      IntegrationType: LAMBDA_FUNCTION
      IntegrationArn: !GetAtt ScreenPop.Arn

ecosystem.title: Agent event stream for WFM
ecosystem.blurb: Adherence needs agent events, not a person refreshing a report. ResourceType AGENT_EVENTS and StorageType KINESIS_STREAM is the hook. A second consumer should read the stream, not a second delivery on the instance.
ecosystem.cfn:
Resources:
  AgentEvents:
    Type: AWS::Connect::InstanceStorageConfig
    Properties:
      InstanceArn: !GetAtt CampusInstance.Arn
      ResourceType: AGENT_EVENTS
      StorageType: KINESIS_STREAM
      KinesisStreamConfig:
        StreamArn: !GetAtt AgentStream.Arn
